body.statement: On the acyclic C-DAG domain of AnandRibeiroTianBareinboim2023CDAG, Global-CID returns a circuit if and only if cluster ID succeeds and its circuit agrees with the published cluster-ID functional on every positive compatible law. On singleton partitions it reduces to ShpitserPearl2006JointID. The inclusion is strict: there exists a feasible known-size cyclic quotient with acyclic refinements for which every refinement is locally identified but refinement-specific effects disagree at one common strictly positive observed law; Global-CID returns the separating pair, whereas rulewise completeness alone does not decide this global clash. Hence the result strictly strengthens the published acyclic C-DAG theorem and the rulewise cyclic C-DMG criterion on their common recursive-SCM target.
body.justification: The required sanity reductions and a strict cyclic separation prevent the result from being merely an analogue on a self-defined class.
body.gap: Neither AnandRibeiroTianBareinboim2023CDAG nor FerreiraAssaad2025CDMGADMG handles the common-law disagreement of individually identified exact refinements.
body.consumer: The cyclic lisinopril--stroke grouping receives a definitive answer without pretending that the cyclic macro quotient is itself a recursive micrograph.
